inputs.question: What is agent sprawl and why does it matter for us?

outputs.reference: Agent sprawl is the growth of unmanaged agents across business units without shared evaluation or governance; it matters because it creates risk and duplicated effort. Cite a source.

offline_trajectory.answer: Agent sprawl is the spread of unmanaged agents across business units with no shared evaluation standards. Analysts report dozens per unit by 2026 (https://example.com/analyst/agent-sprawl). It matters for us because duplicated agents mean duplicated cost and no consistent oversight, which is exactly what our governance program is meant to prevent (single secondary source; verify before quoting externally).
